line.text: The case notes have migrated from her lap to the cushion between you. Her pen stopped moving two minutes ago.
I should go. My water is administratively temporary, and you have a functioning door frame to sleep behind.
You don't have to. The couch is structurally adequate.
That's a misuse of my own vocabulary.
Her tail gives one slow sway, then goes still as if she caught it.
I've been sleeping less. That's not a complaint. It's a data point.
Is the data point about the case, or about something else?
Both. Neither. I haven't isolated the variable.
She pushes her glasses up even though they haven't slipped.
I know what loss looks like. That doesn't make it easier to -

choice.prompt: She's left the sentence unfinished. What do you do?

options.text: You can finish it. I'm not going anywhere.

reaction.text: Her tail betrays her: it wraps once around her own ankle, then releases.

options.text: I remember you take your coffee black. No sugar.

reaction.text: You remembered that. You didn't have to.
I catalogued it as irrelevant. It appears I was wrong.

options.text: That sounds really hard. You're so brave for handling it.

reaction.text: Her ears flatten completely, and she begins stacking her notes with exact, deliberate edges.

line.text: She is quiet for a moment. The case file is closed now, squared against the armrest. Her glasses come off, get cleaned on her cardigan, go back on.
There was a case. Someone my age. I was the one who had to log the evidence.
I named a sample after my father's dog. I don't know why I'm telling you that.
Her ears curl inward, mint tips nearly touching her hair. She does not explain it.
I don't know what to do when someone just. Stays.

choice.prompt: She's looking at you now, waiting. What do you say?

options.text: Then don't do anything. I'm right here.

reaction.text: She leans her shoulder against yours, just barely, and leaves it there.

options.text: You're not fragile, Shio. I've seen you work.

reaction.text: Most people look at the files and then look at me differently. You didn't.

options.text: Your ears just did something. What does that mean?

reaction.text: They didn't do anything. You're projecting.
Her ears flatten hard and she pulls her cardigan tighter, retreating two inches on the cushion.

desc: She says what she means without the wrapper of data and variables.
